summary: A simplified but complete land-development CAD must carry a project from feasibility (parcel, zoning, flood, wetlands, soils, slopes) through survey import, site planning with live zoning and ADA checks, grading with cut/fill balance, hydrology and stormwater sizing, utilities, road and parking geometry, landscape, recordable plats and construction-document sheet sets, to stake-out and as-builts. Today each stage uses two to four tools (Civil 3D with Hydraflow/SSA, Carlson, Trimble Business Center, HydroCAD, Bluebeam, GIS, spreadsheets) joined by DXF/LandXML/CSV/PDF hand-offs where CRS, attributes and references get lost. Must-haves: CRS-aware drawing, COGO points and traverse/mapcheck, parcels with legal descriptions, TIN surfaces with contours and volumes, feature-line grading, Rational/SCS hydrology with Atlas 14 rainfall, pipe networks with crossing checks, alignments and profiles, a parametric zoning rule engine, sheet sets with revision clouds, LandXML/DXF/GeoTIFF/GeoJSON exchange, a project container with link health and provenance, and a never-crash policy. Each old-school and neo technique listed below reduces to a few object types, calculations, data feeds and reports. Nearly all needed US data are public domain or permissive with verified endpoints; OSM (ODbL), NSRDB (CC BY 3.0 US), EPSG (acknowledgement) and ICC code text (copyright) need care. Caveat: the search budget ran out early and official hosts were egress-blocked, so verification came from GitHub code search, AWS open-data registry licence lines and the Autodesk Help API; unverified items are marked.

requirements.feature: Drawing CRS (EPSG), grid-to-ground scale factor, vertical datum tag, reprojection of imports, bearing/azimuth/DMS input, US survey vs international foot
requirements.why: Every survey and data feed is in a different CRS; this is where off-by-a-foot errors come from
requirements.data_source: EPSG dataset via PROJ proj.db; https://epsg.org/terms-of-use.html

requirements.feature: COGO point object (number, N, E, Z, description), point groups, description keys, CSV/PNEZD/LandXML import-export
requirements.why: Survey data enter and leave as points

requirements.feature: Bearing-distance, inverse, intersections, traverse with closure and compass-rule adjustment, mapcheck report
requirements.why: Boundary work and plat checking; reference behaviour is Civil 3D Map Check Report

requirements.feature: Parcel object with area, line/curve tables, lot numbering, ROW parcels, generated metes-and-bounds description with editable phrasing
requirements.why: Plats and legal descriptions are deliverables on every subdivision

requirements.feature: TIN from points, breaklines, contours, GeoTIFF DEM, LandXML; boundaries/holes; contours with interval, index, smoothing, labels; spot elevations; slope/elevation banding
requirements.why: Existing and proposed ground underlie grading, drainage and volumes

requirements.feature: Surface-to-surface volumes (TIN difference) plus grid and average-end-area for reconciliation, labelled by method
requirements.why: Contractors and reviewers compare methods; results differ (Autodesk support note)

requirements.feature: LAS/LAZ point-cloud import with ground-class filtering
requirements.why: 3DEP and drone lidar are the cheapest topo for feasibility

requirements.feature: Feature lines with elevations/grades, slope-to-surface daylight, pad and parking grading, retaining wall TW/BW, live cut/fill balance
requirements.why: Core of site design; model is Civil 3D grading groups

requirements.feature: ADA route checker (running <= 5%, cross <= 2%, ramps <= 1:12 with landings) and accessible parking count from Table 208.2
requirements.why: Plan reviewers reject sets on these; today checked by hand

requirements.feature: Drainage areas with Tc, Rational and SCS-CN runoff (CN from SSURGO HSG), Manning pipe sizing, HGL/EGL on profiles, inlet spread, pond stage-storage-discharge with simple routing
requirements.why: Minimum to produce a drainage report

requirements.feature: NOAA Atlas 14 point fetch stored in the project with provenance
requirements.why: Design storms for every hydrology calc; must not be re-fetched silently

requirements.feature: LID/BMP objects sized to WQv; SWPPP disturbed-area and phasing tally; E&SC symbol library
requirements.why: NPDES construction permits above 1 acre (unverified threshold) and MS4 reviews require them

requirements.feature: Gravity pipe networks (structures, pipes, inverts, slopes, cover, rims), plan/profile labels, crossing and clearance report
requirements.why: Sanitary and storm plans and profiles are mandatory sheets

requirements.feature: Horizontal alignments (tangent, circular curve), stationing, profiles with vertical curves, cross sections
requirements.why: Driveways, streets, utility stationing

requirements.feature: Parametric zoning rule set (setbacks by yard, impervious %, coverage, height, parking ratios, buffers, well/septic/stream setbacks) with live compliance report
requirements.why: Genesis differentiator; done in spreadsheets today and a top source of resubmittals

requirements.feature: Layouts/viewports, sheet index, title-block fields, revision clouds with deltas, north arrow and scale bar objects, match lines, batch PDF with bookmarks
requirements.why: Construction documents are the product

requirements.feature: Plat template (certificates, monument legend, line/curve tables) at recording sizes
requirements.why: Recordable plats have county-specific formats

requirements.feature: DXF/DWG, LandXML 1.2 (surfaces, alignments, profiles, parcels, CgPoints, pipes), GeoJSON/GeoPackage/shapefile, GeoTIFF, CSV, PDF out
requirements.why: Every hand-off in the workflow table uses one of these

requirements.feature: Project container bundling drawing, references and data snapshots with relative paths, link-health check and per-layer provenance (URL, date, licence, attribution)
requirements.why: Stated Genesis goal; ODbL/CC-BY attribution is also a legal need

requirements.feature: Live connectors with caching to NFHL, NWI, SSURGO, 3DEP, Atlas 14, parcels, OSM
requirements.why: Feasibility maps in minutes instead of a GIS detour

requirements.feature: Never-crash policy, autosave/journaling, recovery, hostile-input tests for every parser
requirements.why: Zero-crash goal; parsers of external data are the main risk

requirements.feature: Sun-path/shadow study, PV layout and PVWatts v8 call; rainwater catchment and cistern sizing; septic sizing; defensible-space rings; BFE/freeboard check
requirements.why: Cheap to add on top of surfaces and rules; strong differentiator for owner-builders and permaculture designers

requirements.feature: Spirals, superelevation, corridors/assemblies, least-squares survey adjustment, dynamic routing via EPA SWMM, 3D visualisation
requirements.why: Highway- and survey-firm-grade features; not needed for a first permit set

old_school.what_cad_needs: Bearing/azimuth/DMS parser and formatter; create point/line by bearing-distance; inverse; bearing-bearing and distance-distance intersections; traverse with closure and compass-rule adjustment; mapcheck report
Parcel to description generator (POB, calls, curve radius/arc/chord/delta) with editable phrasing, and a deed-text parser that draws the boundary
Plat templates at recording sizes, lot/block numbering, line and curve tables, found/set monument symbols, easement hatches, certificate and dedication text blocks, vicinity map viewport
TIN with linear interpolation along edges, contour tracing at any interval with index contours and non-crossing smoothing, and an interpolate-between-two-spot-grades command

Own stroke drafting font, lineweight-by-layer matching pen weights, standard civil linetypes (property, easement, centerline, fence, contours), north arrow, graphic scale, match lines, material hatches
Catchment object (roof polygon, pitch, efficiency), downspout routing, cistern object (volume, overflow, first flush), calc gallons = ft2 x inches x 0.623 x efficiency, monthly mass balance vs demand
old_school.source: 0.623 constant e.g. github.com/PDFCraftTool/OmniTools; TWDB Rainwater Harvesting Manual https://www.twdb.texas.gov/publications/brochures/conservation/doc/RainwaterHarvestingManual_3rdedition.pdf (unverified)

old_school.what_cad_needs: Below-grade structure object with earth-cover depth, frost-depth check, vent stacks, drain-to-daylight, auto section view

Sun-path diagram and solar altitude/azimuth for date and place (implement Reda-Andreas SPA from the NREL report, not NREL's C code), long-axis orientation check, overhang depth from sun angles, shadow casting from terrain/trees/neighbours
old_school.source: NREL/TP-560-34302 as transcribed in pvlib spa.py (github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python); https://www.energy.gov/energysaver/passive-solar-home-design (unverified)

old_school.what_cad_needs: Trace-contour-at-elevation, near-contour polylines draped on surface with a set fall (keyline ~1:400), terrace spacing from slope, swale cross-section cut/fill, spillway points
old_school.source: NRCS CPS 600/412/362 (CPS numbering confirmed via github.com/HiCSC/ClimateSmartPracticeStandards); Yeomans keyline (unverified)

key_claims.claim: Civil 3D 2026 ships Hydraflow Storm Sewers, Hydrographs (SCS and Rational, pond routing) and Express (culverts, channels, inlets, weirs) plus Storm and Sanitary Analysis as extensions
Civil 3D grading auto-balance iterates toward a target net volume with a 0.1% tolerance and may need re-running
Civil 3D survey import accepts field book, LandXML, point files and drawing points; linework depends on description keys, linework code sets and figure prefix databases
Civil 3D mapcheck reports closure, perimeter, area and curve data with POB choice, direction of travel and chord-vs-arc options; legal-description phrasing lives in an XML file
NOAA Atlas 14 point estimates are served by a CGI endpoint used in many public clients; Atlas 15 began as a 2024 Montana pilot with CONUS estimates in peer review in 2026
USGS 3DEP products are public domain and the TNM Access API returns tile lists for the 1 m DEM and LPC datasets
FEMA NFHL MapServer layer 28 carries FLD_ZONE, SFHA_TF and ZONE_SUBTY
SSURGO map-unit hydrologic soil group is muaggatt.hydgrpdcd, queryable with T-SQL via Soil Data Access
2021 IRC has Appendices AS (straw bale), AR (light straw-clay) and AU (cob); 2024 IRC adds Appendix BL (hempcrete) as non-structural infill requiring local adoption
2010 ADA Standards Table 208.2 scopes accessible spaces by lot size and one in six accessible spaces must be van-accessible
